content.comment_body: Hello, When the working hours exceed 65535 (about 1092 hours and 15 minutes), the cell shows 'unsupported data', likely due to a data length limitation in LWE. In [product_name] V8.3.0, there's a block with variable memory configuration ('hour counter', parameter 'OT', type 'Dword'). The LWE version used was [version_no]. Has this problem been addressed in newer LWE releases?
Displaying the value in LWE for Words as an analog value isn’t correct. You should use the 'Scaled Time' function for proper display.
Check this topic: Visualising actual hour counter values in LWE. My post on the second page from 10/15/2022 6:07 AM provides more details.

A DWORD can't be directly shown as hours and minutes on screen. Also, don't count on bugs getting fixed quickly in LWE – on Linux, LWE crashes about every fifth or sixth save; on Windows, this is less frequent. The software has quite a few bugs and glitches, which can be frustrating. I spent several months building the project shown below using LWE. Note: In another language: Ausalt, ma tean, mida räägin. Vaata või saksakeelset foorumi osa.
Actually, you can do this. See the attached screen capture for demonstration.

That's right, I had forgotten. I recall one case with a compressor timeout, where the value was set in seconds but I needed to display minutes and seconds instead. The solution in the end was similar.
I’m not sure why my results look as they do in the uploaded screenshots.
I suggest updating your software. There’s an update from [version_no] to [version_no] and from LWE [version_no] to [version_no]. Installation instructions are available at [url].
Upload your LWE project here and I’ll try it with LWE [version_no] and [version_no].

Here's an example file with hour counters (and a weekly timer) for [product_name] ([version_no]) and [product_name] ([version_no]). I'll install the latest versions of both programs soon for further review. If the new LWE version fixes the issue, this topic can be considered resolved.
Hour meter readings now display correctly on the webpage when using LWE [version_no]. The issue is resolved.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face a display issue in [product_name] [version_no] when hour counters exceed 65535, leading to 'unsupported data' due to a data length limit. Confusion exists about how to show larger hour values, with users frustrated by frequent crashes, especially on Linux. The need to use the correct display function ('Scaled Time') rather than analog value for such counters is pointed out, and updating to [version_no] is suggested as a solution.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to accurately display large hour counts (>65535) in the web interface without errors, and handle DWORD time counters reliably. Stability across different operating systems and timely bug resolution are also expected.
